types.name: lesson
types.records: something learned from experience that changes how we work next time
types.use_when: a mistake, a slow round or a surprise taught us a better way of working

types.name: gotcha
types.records: a surprising behaviour of a tool, library, platform or environment that trips you even when you do things "right"
types.use_when: a tool did something unexpected (a flag needs a full SHA, a hook drops output in sub-agents)

types.name: edgecase
types.records: a specific boundary input or state the code or the spec must handle
types.use_when: a review or test found an input at the edge (empty, max, encoding, race window)

types.name: constraint
types.records: a hard limit imposed from outside that bounds every choice
types.use_when: the owner, a law, a platform, a budget or a compatibility promise fixes something

types.name: contract
types.records: an agreed interface or behaviour that other parts or third parties rely on (API, schema, protocol, file format, module boundary)
types.use_when: a contract is created, changed or clarified

types.name: adr
types.records: an architectural decision record: a choice that shapes the system's structure (stack, module boundaries, data model, protocols, security model)
types.use_when: an architectural choice is made or reversed

types.name: edr
types.records: an execution decision record: a choice about how to carry the work out (implementation approach, process or operational call) — not architecture
types.use_when: the lead, owner or an agent chose how to do something
must_contain: the steps if it is a procedure

types.name: outcome
types.records: the factual result of an action, task, train or run
must_contain: where the evidence is — no opinion

types.name: trap
types.records: a tempting approach that looks right but leads to failure
types.use_when: a design or process idea failed, or would fail, for a non-obvious reason

types.name: heuristic
types.records: a rule of thumb that usually works
types.use_when: you found a reliable shortcut for estimating, choosing or prioritising

types.name: invariant
types.records: a property that must always hold
types.use_when: a guarantee the system or process relies on is identified
must_contain: the test or check that proves it

types.name: goal
types.records: a desired result with success criteria
types.use_when: a milestone, task or project objective is set

types.name: nogoal
types.use_when: the owner or lead rules something out, to prevent scope creep

types.name: requirement
types.records: something the product or process must do
types.use_when: the owner or a spec states a need

types.name: deferred
types.use_when: work is moved later on purpose
must_contain: the trigger or date to revisit

types.name: security
types.records: a security-relevant fact: threat, weakness, control, secret-handling rule or security finding
types.use_when: a threat or weakness is found, a control is added or changed, a security review concludes

types.name: bug
types.records: a defect found in the product or the tooling (not a third-party tool's surprise: gotcha; not a boundary the spec must handle: edgecase)
types.use_when: a defect is found, reproduced or fixed
must_contain: the regression test that pins it

recall_moments.search_for: the task id, the module/component names, the files it will touch

recall_moments.when: an error, a failing test, a refused command, anything surprising
recall_moments.search_for: the error text, tool name, symptom words

recall_moments.when: before taking a decision (design or execution)
before changing a contract, schema or public behaviour
recall_moments.search_for: the contract id, the surface, the consumers
